analysis.title: European Leaders: Equity recommendations (CIO Equity Selection List)
key_insights: UBS CIO removed Deutsche Bank from the European Leaders selection list, the only change in this edition. The stated reason is better alternatives elsewhere, and the investment banking cycle recovery and German macro benefit may take longer to materialize than previously expected.

The list is built around five themes: Industry 4.0 and Automation, Defense and Infrastructure, Decarbonization, Demographics and Consumers, and Financing structural reforms. The benchmark is MSCI EMU.
CIO expects European earnings growth to accelerate, supported by fiscal expansion, policy reforms, and structural drivers (AI, power and resources, longevity).

Theme portfolio weights: Demographics and Consumers 15.0% (unchanged), Defence and Infrastructure 14.0% (from 12.0%, +2.0%), Financing structural reforms 31.0% (from 35.0%, -4.0%), Industry 4.0 and Automation 22.0%, Decarbonization 18.0% (from 16.0%, +2.0%). Stocks within a sub-theme are equal-weighted.

Industry 4.0: recent PMI surveys show the manufacturing index reaching 50 for the first time in three years. CIO expects fiscal stimulus and the shift toward smart manufacturing to support the next industrial cycle.

Defense: Europe is entering a major defense and infrastructure investment cycle driven by the Russia-Ukraine conflict and NATO spending targets of 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core defense, 1.5% defense- and security-related). A NATO review is scheduled for 2029.
Decarbonization: renewables were 47% of Europe's power generation mix in 2024. The EU targets climate neutrality by 2050.
Demographics: nearly 20% of Europeans are over 65 versus 10% globally. Health care spending per capita for the over-65s is three times that of working-age individuals.

Financing reforms: the Draghi report puts the annual investment needed for the EU reform agenda at about 5% of GDP through 2030. The Savings and Investment Union aims to deepen capital markets and revive securitization.

ASML: CIO says the market is over-discounting cyclical fears and sees the current valuation as an attractive entry point. It expects tight memory supply/demand and elevated memory spot prices to persist on AI demand and DRAM-to-HBM capacity conversion. Risk: order push-outs or cancellations if consumer semiconductor or AI memory end-markets weaken.

ASM International: CIO expects growth in FY26 to accelerate into FY27 as the 2nm ramp and gate-all-around transition drive ALD and epitaxy adoption. Risks are a smaller-than-expected 2nm node, market share loss, and a macro slowdown.

Infineon: CIO believes non-AI estimates are largely derisked and data center revenue should reach a mid-teens percentage of group revenue by FY27. It warns that beating expectations without a guidance upgrade may not unlock further upside.

SAP: CIO sees the dislocation in the shares due to AI concerns as an attractive entry point. About 40% of clients have upgraded, legacy ERP support ends at the end of 2027, and top-line growth is expected to peak around 2027-28.

Ferrari: 3Q26 results were good with a further upgrade of full-year revenue guidance across all metrics. Plug-in hybrids were 42% of FY25 shipments and 33% in 3Q26. The order book extends into 2028, and the EUR 550k first fully electric model appears covered for 2027.

Richemont: Jewellery Maisons grew 14% in the latest results, led by Cartier. The stock trades at 20-year relative lows versus peers on P/E, and CIO sees valuation as appealing after share price underperformance.
Lonza: CIO is increasing exposure to European health care, which has lagged in recent months. It expects high-single-digit industry growth and margin recovery in 2026/27.

Banks: Barclays has a CET1 ratio of 14.3% and SocGen 13.2% in 2Q26 (above its 13% excess-capital threshold, with a 50% payout commitment). Standard Chartered trades at 1.4x tangible book with a path to 15% return on tangible equity and an upcoming capital markets day as a potential catalyst.

Raiffeisen: CIO sees the stock as volatile but likes improving core trends, 7% y/y loan growth guidance for 2026, and a potential beneficiary of a Russia-Ukraine peace deal or a positive Russian deconsolidation outcome.

Erste: CIO sees the Santander Polska acquisition (49% stake) as a positive catalyst not reflected in valuation. Santander: delivered or exceeded targets for a fourth year, with a 2028 return on tangible equity target above 20%, and the Webster and TSB integrations as the next catalysts.

Rheinmetall: CIO sees double-digit annual earnings growth until the end of the decade possible from German defense equipment spending. Risks are delayed orders, lower spending, a shift of spending to US firms, and unclear financing. It expects higher sector volatility.
Rolls-Royce: turnaround case with 2028 targets of EBIT GBP 3.6-3.9bn and FCF GBP 4.2-4.5bn, trading at an attractive FCF yield versus aerospace peers, and a new share buyback program.

Airbus: attractive on NTM EV/EBIT, with a multi-year backlog and rising production rates supporting earnings growth above the European industrials average through the end of the decade. Risks include delivery ramp-up delays and euro appreciation versus the dollar.

Holcim: P/E of 18.4x is below its 15-year average. CIO thinks guidance is too conservative and consensus too low after 1H26 results exceeded full-year guidance. Sika: CIO sees scope for earnings upgrades as construction passes its trough in 2026 and MBCC synergies materialize.
Enel guides EPS of EUR 0.72-0.74 in 2026 and EUR 0.80-0.82 in 2028, with about EUR 53bn of capex for 2026-2028 (EUR 10bn above the prior plan) and a EUR 3.5bn buyback.
RWE plans EUR 35bn of investment for 2026-31 and targets 12% EPS CAGR for 2026-31, with a EUR 1.32 per share dividend planned for FY2026. Capacity should rise from about 38GW to 65GW by 2031.

Schneider Electric, Legrand, Prysmian and Siemens Energy are positioned on AI data center, grid and electrification demand. Siemens Energy trades at a discount to US peers, with a gas-turbine market seen tight into 2030.

Siemens is on a de-conglomeration path, including a planned spin-off of 30% of Siemens Healthineers to Siemens shareholders (stake was 67% as of 12 November 2025, guided below 20% medium term). CIO sees an unjustified sum-of-the-parts discount.

Methodology: effective 1 November 2026 CIO no longer rates or ranks equities and no longer publishes top picks. 'CIO Selected' is a designation, not a rating, and does not create a price target or modify the UBS Investment Bank rating.

sector_views.rationale: Portfolio weight raised to 14.0% from 12.0%. Structural spending driven by NATO targets and the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Portfolio weight raised to 18.0% from 16.0%. Grid, power demand and data center electrification support growth.
Theme weight cut to 31.0% from 35.0% after Deutsche Bank removal. Banks seen as inexpensive with capital return potential.
CIO is increasing exposure to European health care, which has lagged in recent months.
Industry 4.0 theme carries a 22.0% weight. Manufacturing PMI reached 50 for the first time in three years.

earnings_insights: Ferrari 3Q26 results (reported) were good, with full-year revenue guidance upgraded across all metrics.
Richemont latest results (reported): Jewellery Maisons sales up 14%, led by Cartier on US and European consumers.
Holcim 1H26 results (reported) came in above full-year guidance, and CIO considers guidance too conservative and consensus too low.
Enel company guidance: EPS EUR 0.72-0.74 in 2026 and EUR 0.80-0.82 in 2028, EPS CAGR of about 6% from 2025 to 2030 (guidance, not reported).
RWE company target: 12% EPS CAGR for 2026-31, with a planned FY2026 dividend of EUR 1.32 per share (target).
Rolls-Royce company targets for 2028: EBIT GBP 3.6-3.9bn and FCF GBP 4.2-4.5bn (targets, not reported).
Raiffeisen management guides for 7% y/y loan growth in 2026 (guidance).

Infineon: CIO expects data center revenue at a mid-teens percentage of group revenue by FY27 (CIO estimate). Operational expectations are elevated, so an earnings beat without a guidance upgrade may not be enough.
Santander: 2Q26 and prior results not quantified. Company has met or exceeded targets for four years in a row and targets return on tangible equity above 20% in 2028 (target).

macro_indicators.interpretation: First reading at 50 in three years, which CIO reads as a signal of manufacturing expansion supporting Industry 4.0 names.

macro_indicators.reading: 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core defense plus 1.5% defense- and security-related)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a multi-year European defense and infrastructure investment cycle. A NATO review is scheduled for 2029.
Needs private savings mobilization through the Savings and Investment Union, supportive for European banks and capital markets.

macro_indicators.indicator: Renewables share of European power generation
macro_indicators.interpretation: Share is set to rise further, supporting electrification and utility names.
Supports demand in health care, consumer health and luxury.

risk_factors: Macro slowdown hitting equipment demand (ASML, ASM International) and order push-outs from weak consumer semiconductor or AI memory end-markets.
Euro appreciation versus the US dollar (Airbus, Ferrari and others).
Delayed defense orders, lower-than-expected spending, a shift of spending to US firms, and unclear financing for European defense (Rheinmetall).
Slowdown in data center capex (Schneider Electric, Siemens Energy, Legrand).
Slower AI-related pricing model changes and software seat reduction (SAP).
Credit cycle, interest rate and regulatory risks for banks, including the FCA motor finance review (Barclays).
Wealth destruction hitting high-end demand and brand reception of the first electric model (Ferrari).
Chinese competition in power semiconductors (Infineon) and mixed Chinese sales trends (Sika).
Negative news flow on the Russian business (Raiffeisen).
vol_and_positioning: Rheinmetall: CIO expects news flow to remain fluid, increasing volatility for the sector and the stock.
Raiffeisen: CIO says shares are likely to remain volatile.
Richemont trades at 20-year relative lows versus peers on P/E.
Siemens Energy trades at a significant discount to US peers on a range of valuation multiples.
geopolitical: Russia-Ukraine conflict drives the European defense spending cycle.
NATO summit targets of 3.5% core defense plus 1.5% related spending by 2035, with a 2029 review.
Possible Russia-Ukraine peace deal named as a potential benefit for Raiffeisen Bank International.
Raiffeisen's Russian exit plans have been blocked by authorities or challenged in court.
Geopolitical situation and Middle East demand cited as a risk for Ferrari.
US tariffs cited as a risk for Ferrari (price increases of up to 10% announced) and as a tailwind for Prysmian's US manufacturing.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-AI estimates are derisked and data center revenue should reach a mid-teens percentage of group revenue by FY27, letting Infineon outperform medium-term growth expectations.
tension_points.bear_case: Expectations are elevated, so beating them without a guidance upgrade may not unlock further upside, and the automotive recovery could be slower than anticipated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A beat without a guidance upgrade, or a slower-than-expected automotive recovery.

tension_points.bull_case: Market is over-discounting cyclical fears. Memory tightness and DRAM-to-HBM conversion support multiyear capacity additions.
tension_points.bear_case: Deterioration in consumer semiconductor or AI memory end-markets can lead to order push-outs or cancellations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weakness in consumer macroeconomic data points and order push-outs or cancellations.

tension_points.bear_case: Delayed orders, lower-than-expected spending, a shift toward US firms, and unresolved financing could hurt the sector.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delayed defense orders or lower-than-expected spending, with a NATO review scheduled for 2029.
